title: Path steering schema validator and staggered launch plan
content:
Overview

This note captures a proposed validator and staggered launch (aka staggered canary) process for our routing rule configuration schema (JSON/YAML) — internal name: "path-steering". The goal: give a low-friction, auditable path for schema changes and policy rollouts across multi-region control planes while minimizing user impact and providing automated rollback signals.

Why a new validator/flow?
- We have multiple parallel efforts touching route semantics (region priority, cost steering, fallbacks, model-variant mapping). Small schema changes have caused subtle serving mismatches.
- Current gating is manual and ad-hoc: reviews + monitoring. We need repeatable, machine-checkable gates plus a safe progressive rollout.

High level proposal
1) Introduce a path-steering schema validator service (CLI + server) that runs in CI and as a pre-apply hook in control-plane.
2) Support compatibility levels: strict | compat | additive-only.
3) Provide an automated staggered launch orchestrator that can push rules to increasing percentage buckets (per-region, per-customer-tier) and evaluate defined health signals.
4) Enforce automatic rollback on sustained violations with postmortem artifacts.

Schema: example and notes
- We keep configuration as YAML/JSON; the validator normalizes both. The schema is intentionally ergonomic for product authors: pattern-matching routes, percentages, model variants, and routing predicates.

Example YAML (author-facing):

---
version: 1.2
metadata:
  name: path-steer-2025-02-10
  owner: eng/platform-priya
  description: steer text-generation requests for retail region traffic to cheaper model variants with fallback to high-availability variant
rules:
  - id: region-steer-eu
    match: "request.region == 'eu'"
    priority: 10
    actions:
      - type: weighted-variants
        variants:
          - model: redwood-3b-q4
            weight: 80
          - model: redwood-3b-ptx
            weight: 20
    constraints:
      latency_slo_ms: 200
      allowed_regions: [eu, uk]
  - id: fallback-on-llm-error
    match: "response.status in ['error','timeout']"
    priority: 1
    actions:
      - type: failover
        to_variant: redwood-3b-ptx
---

Key schema considerations
- version: semantic for schema evolution. Validator supports migration hints for 1.x -> 2.x.
- rules[] order is not relied upon; priority determines evaluation order.
- actions: typed union (weighted-variants, failover, rewrite-headers, cache-bypass). Validator rejects unknown types unless compatibility level allows additive extensions.
- match expressions: evaluated in sandboxed expression engine (limited ops). The validator statically checks references to request/response fields and flags unsafe or non-cost-bounded expressions.

Validator behavior and checks
- Syntax + schema conformance (required keys, correct types).
- Semantic checks:
  - Percentages sum to <= 100 for weighted-variants; warn if < 100 (implicit passthrough).
  - Variant existence check: model referenced must exist in model registry (via ENVs or model-catalog API).
  - Region scoping: requested allowed_regions entries must be valid region tokens.
  - Priority collisions: two rules with exactly same match and same priority emit a collision warning.
  - Safety heuristics: match expressions must not call network or blocking ops; only allow field accesses and arithmetic/comparisons.
  - Resource impact estimate: quick static estimator for expected KV-cache size and approximate token cost influence. This is a conservative heuristic used for gating heavy changes.

Compatibility Modes
- strict: reject any unknown top-level keys or action types; intended for stable prod branches.
- compat: accept additive new keys but emit warnings and record telemetry; used on staging.
- additive-only: only allow additions, not breaking renames; used for rapid iteration branches.

Rollout mechanics (staggered launch)
- Buckets available: per-region, per-customer-tier (free/premium), per-deployment (hosted/dedicated).
- Default plan: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with observation windows between steps. Windows: 15m -> 30m -> 1h -> 2h -> 4h. These are tunable per-rule.
- Automated checks at each step:
  - Error rate (5xx / total) delta threshold: +0.5% absolute or +150% relative, whichever tripped first.
  - Latency P95 increase: > 15% or > 100ms absolute.
  - Cost unit delta (estimated token cost): > 8% increase.
  - Quality signals: if available, small evaluation set regression (e.g., reranker or prompt set) above configured threshold.
- If any check fails, immediate rollback to previous bucket and alerting. If failures persist for 2 consecutive rollbacks on distinct metrics, block rollout and require human review.

Observability hooks and metrics
- Tag all requests by rollout-id and bucket. Persist sample traces (1 in 200) for deeper investigation.
- Export metrics: rollout_error_rate_delta, rollout_latency_delta_p95, rollout_cost_delta, rollout_quality_regression.
- Push aggregated metrics to Redwood Console and to a temporary named dashboard per rollout.

Control plane interactions
- The control plane accepts a validated artifact (manifest + signature). The pre-apply hook calls the validator and then uploads manifest to control plane staging namespace with a rollout-plan metadata block.
- Control plane operator endpoints: 
  - POST /manifests -> returns rollout-id
  - POST /rollouts/{id}/advance -> requests next bucket
  - POST /rollouts/{id}/abort -> immediate rollback
- Rollout orchestration can be manual (button in Console) or automated (CI pipeline). The orchestrator enforces observation windows.

CI integration: suggested pipeline
1) developer creates PR with schema changes + unit tests for validator (match expression cases, percentage heuristics). 2) GH action runs: unit tests -> schema validator in compat mode -> integration run that spins up a small staging canary. 3) If pass, migration build attaches signed manifest and posts to control-plane staging for manual or automated staggered launch.

Preflight checklist (what the validator and flow should enforce):
- [ ] Schema passed (no fatal errors)
- [ ] No unknown action types in strict mode
- [ ] Models referenced exist and are pinned or have fallback
- [ ] Observation window and thresholds set (or default applied)
- [ ] Rollback policy defined (immediate -> previous bucket -> abort)
- [ ] Linked evaluation prompt set attached (if quality-safety sensitive)

Multi-region nuances and eventual consistency
- Replication lag: control-plane uses eventual replication. Rollouts should be region-aware: if a rule targets EU only, we start EU buckets independently and only expand global buckets after regional stability.
- Partial failure model: if region A advances but region B fails to apply manifest due to transient control-plane issues, we treat that as a partial rollout and do not progress global buckets.
- Failover guidance: for cross-region fallbacks (e.g., eu -> us fallback), the validator flags potential data residency/security issues and requires an allowlist flag.

Rollback and postmortem automation
- On rollback, capture: manifest diff, representative traces, metric deltas, and last successful bucket. Attach to rollout record (rollout-id).
- Trigger an automated postmortem template (link in Confluence) if rollback was triggered by > 2 buckets or service impact > 5 minutes.

Edge cases and open questions
- How to represent complex weighted distributions that condition on request attributes (e.g., user-tier + session-length)? Initial approach: disallow nested conditionals in variant weights; instead authors compose rules with higher priorities.
- When model catalog is updated (rename/deprecate), how to auto-migrate manifests referencing old names? Proposal: provide a schema-migrator tool that can rewrite manifests with mappings from a migration table. Requires human approval.
- Canary fragmentation: too many tiny buckets for many small customers can create metric noise. Consider grouping small customers into a single synthetic bucket for observability.

Operational runbook (brief)
- Failure observed during rollout step:
  1) System triggers rollback to previous bucket automatically.
  2) Pager on-call SRE + owning engineer.
  3) Run the validator locally against live traffic sample with --simulate option to replicate.
  4) If rollback insufficient, escalate to manual abort and open incident.

Next steps (action items)
- Build minimal validator prototype (schema + static checks) and wire to GH actions. Owner: Miguel. Target: 2025-03-15.
- Implement rollout orchestration MVP in control plane (advance/abort endpoints + tagging). Owner: Rohit. Target: 2025-04-01.
- Write migration docs for model-catalog renames and region allowlists. Owner: Anya. Target: 2025-03-22.

Notes to self / TODOs (brainstorm)
- Add quick-fuzz harness for match expressions to find pathological matches.
- Consider a safe whitelist for match expression functions (no regex backtracking allowed).
- Add more guardrails for cost-sensitive customers (e.g., tiered budget checks).
